definition: An attack in which an adversary queries a deployed model repeatedly to reconstruct a functionally similar copy of it.
details: Model extraction attacks threaten the intellectual property and security of proprietary models served via APIs, motivating rate limiting and query monitoring as defenses.

explainer.lead: An attacker queries a deployed model repeatedly to rebuild a functionally similar copy. This threatens the intellectual property and security of proprietary models served through APIs.

tiers.eli5: It is like asking a chef hundreds of questions about a secret recipe until you can cook nearly the same dish yourself.
tiers.practitioner: Defenders watch query patterns and apply rate limiting because extraction needs many queries. A pitfall is that tight limits hurt legitimate heavy users, so thresholds must be tuned against real traffic.
tiers.paperLevel: The attack reconstructs a model by fitting a surrogate to input-output pairs from the target; fidelity depends on query budget and access to outputs or probabilities. Known limits: cost scales with query count, and defenses such as rate limiting and query monitoring raise the bar rather than eliminate the risk.

explainer.example: An adversary sends thousands of labeled queries to a hosted classifier and trains a local model that matches most of its predictions, capturing much of its behavior without the original weights.
